1.note: A sound play: פִּרְדֵי (mules) and הַפְּרִידָה (parting) share the root letters פ־ר־ד.

2.note: After Ezek 43:2 "the earth shone with his glory". הֲלֹם means "here, hither"; מֵהִלָּם is read as "from where they were". The pointing could also suggest a form of הלם "to strike" (dazzled).

3.note: בָּרֹד is "dappled" (Gen 31:10) and בָּרָד is "hail". Read as a cheek white as hail; "spotted" (with a beauty mark) is also possible.

4.note: מַלְקוֹחַיִם is the jaws or palate (Ps 22:16). The drops from the teeth (the "crystal") are her saliva, sweet as honey from the comb (Prov 16:24 צוּף דְּבַשׁ).

5.note: A play on שַׁחַר (dawn) and שָׁחוֹר (black): the face is so bright that the dawn looks dark beside it.

6.note: Literally "like the day". Read as an echo of Mal 3:19 "the day comes, burning like an oven". It can also mean "as this day", that is, now.

7.note: סְעִיפִים are boughs or clefts. The "pomegranates" under the veils are probably the breasts (or the cheeks, as in Song 4:3); the exact image is uncertain.

8.note: The words of Ruth 4:16 ("and became his nurse"). "Them" seems to be the stars: the soul is so high that it nurses the stars. The reference is uncertain.

9.note: Ruth 4:4, the kinsman's right to redeem. Heman claims that the right to ask about every secret is his alone.

10.note: A play: לְבָנָה "white" (feminine adjective) and לְבָנָה "the moon" are written the same.

11.note: No-amon (Nah 3:8) is Egyptian Thebes. Medieval Jewish writers often took it to be Alexandria.

12.note: A play on צֹעַן (Zoan, Tanis in Egypt) and the verb צען "to move a tent, wander" (Isa 33:20). The next pair plays the same way on נֹף (Noph, Memphis) and יְפֵה נוֹף ("beautiful in height", Mount Zion, Ps 48:3).
